body:
I recently updated my system (Arch Linux, Hyprland) and something must have changed on the Wayland side relatively recently. Cant pinpoint this further than that unfortunately.

In my game debugger window the mouse also starts bugging out. The cursor will default to the OS one. Instead of my custom ones.

Also, the window starts going down to 1 FPS after a while and doesn't recover. Can't make anything out in the profiler. This might be entirely on my end though.

Also running arch + hyprland, the mouse works fine when toggling fullscreen mode.
It used to work on the same Godot version before (I have a mono 4.5.1 and  regular4.4.1). 
The only thing that changed was making a full system update.
Also facing this problem on arch + hyprland. It almost works in the single window mode, except for the script editors where selection with a mouse still has an offset
Just follow up to say that I updated my system today and the problem is gone, they were wayland related packages in the update

> Just follow up to say that I updated my system today and the problem is gone, they were wayland related packages in the update

System update didn't fix the issue for me unfortunately, can you share your arch and wayland version?
Although I found a workaround, steam version with the exact same settings doesn't have this issue for some reason

> Just follow up to say that I updated my system today and the problem is gone, they were wayland related packages in the update

I updated Arch + Hyprland today and it didn't solve the issue. Can you confirm your are running it with the `Prefer Wayland` option on?

Yes running with prefer wayland + single Window Mode turned On.
run configuration that works now:
```
Godot Engine v4.5.1.stable.mono.arch_linux - https://godotengine.org
OpenGL API 4.6 (Core Profile) Mesa 25.2.7-arch1.1 - Compatibility - Using Device: AMD - AMD Radeon 680M (radeonsi, rembrandt, LLVM 21.1.5, DRM 3.64, 6.17.9-arch1-1)
```

Listing some versions of packages intalled on my side:
wayland 1.24.0-1
wayland-protocols 1.46-1
linux-firmware 20251125-1
linux-firmware-amdgpu 20251125-1
linux 6.17.9.arch1-1
hyprland 0.52.1-6

Hope this help
`Single Window Mode` did the trick. Although, I'd like a proper solution without forcing the Single Window Mode.

I am also having the issues (mouse position being offset and game becoming almost unresponsive after a window resize)

Tried both Prefer Wayland and Single Window Mode on. I tried all combinations actually.
Unfortunately this did not seem to help on my end. I wonder if I am missing something. I am fairly new to Linux desktop, so I would hate to provide false information here.

My versions seem quite similar to what was mentioned above:
godot 4.5.1.stable.arch_linux
wayland 1.24.0-1
wayland-protocols 1.46-1
linux-firmware 20251125-1
linux-firmware-amdgpu 20251125-1
linux 6.17.9.arch1-1
hyprland 0.52.1-6

Can confirm I'm also having this issue. @deralmas is this something you would be wanting to take a look at?

I also added some additional context in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/107435#issuecomment-3600386170 (didn't realize this bug report existed before typing all that on the pull request, my apologies.)

But a quick recap of my findings from there and since then:

- Happens only on Wayland + Hyprland (tried in Wayland + Niri and it's working just fine there)
- I think I confirmed it didn't have anything to do with fractional scaling (since it works in Niri and not in Wayland, and both have fractional scaling; also disabled fractional scaling on Hyprland and the issue still persisted).
- Also happens for any dropdowns in the various sidebars.
- This does not occur for me on Godot 4.5.1 when enabling Wayland, but it does on the latest 4.6 dev 5 release.

(I am using the direct downloads/executables in all situations as opposed to the AUR packaged version as mentioned from the OP. I'm also using CachyOS ((Arch Linux)), in case there's an impact there.)

Hi, thank you for your reports! Could anybody please record a protocol dump while replicating this issue?
To get a full dump + verbose log, you can run the editor like this:

```sh
WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 path/to/godot --verbose path/to/project.godot 2>&1 | tee debug.log
```

Please note that, during this process, all input sent to the editor/game will be part of the log, so please don't write anything sensitive in there (you shouldn't need to).

> `GODOT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_EMBEDDER=1 path/to/godot path/to/project.godot`

I just gave this a shot. It does **not** fix it.

(Didn't try the code changes bits because I suck at git.)

> I just gave this a shot. It does not fix it.

That's good news, the embedder is a pretty complex beast, if the issue was there it would have been very annoying trust me xD

> (Didn't try the code changes bits because I suck at git.)

It's a one line change, just look for `if (libdecor_found) {` in the code and add an `&& false` in the condition, so that it's never true. That will skip the initialization logic.

Okay I gave it a shot! `git clone git@github.com:godotengine/godot.git` Edited the code here: `scons platform=linuxbsd` It's working! https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61794adb-c5ad-4a3f-b0ab-cec55f8f0686 Which, I suppose ultimately isn't good news since this libdecor stuff is busted? 😟 Attached a fresh `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1` log here in case it's at all useful. [debug2.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24012858/debug2.log)

Also, if relevant/useful, there's also some weird blinking/flashing happening where the popup was previously, it's mostly visible after you click to close the popup, but it seems to happen throughout.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca835849-7239-4c40-8155-a818e1929739

> Which, I suppose ultimately isn't good news since this libdecor stuff is busted? 😟

It's not that bad of a news. Actually, if the issue is in libdecor that's actually great, as it's dynamically linked so once the system fixes it it should retroactively fix itself :D

Assuming that it's a libdecor issue of course. It could be the Wayland backend, libdecor, a libdecor plugin or the compositor itself.

> Also, if relevant/useful, there's also some weird blinking/flashing happening where the popup was previously, it's mostly visible after you click to close the popup, but it seems to happen throughout.

The flashing is weird. I don't think that it's relevant to this issue.

Also, we don't do this kind of fading, so I guess that it's the compositor being funny. Maybe it's related to the popup surfaces (probably) using Vulkan?

Aight, this looks like a known libdecor bug:

 - https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/libdecor/libdecor/-/issues/80
 - https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/libdecor/libdecor/-/issues/81

It got fixed in a commit, and will be fixed in the latest **libdecor** release. Right now there's no way to disable it at runtime (outside of somehow hiding it from the library path), so the simplest way might be to just downgrade to libdecor 0.2.3.

> Aight, this looks like a known libdecor bug:
> 
> * https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/libdecor/libdecor/-/issues/80
> * https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/libdecor/libdecor/-/issues/81
> 
> It got fixed in a commit, and will be fixed in the latest **libdecor** release. Right now there's no way to disable it at runtime (outside of somehow hiding it from the library path), so the simplest way might be to just downgrade to libdecor 0.2.3.

Incredible! Appreciate it very much!
Can confirm that the issue was fixed in libdecor 0.2.5-1. Works nicely for me both in single and multi window mode

Awesome! Also, if for whatever reason you won't be able to update, I want to announce that #96825 got merged, which adds a new environment variable: `GODOT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_LIBDECOR`. If set to exactly `1`, it won't load and initialize libdecor, which should fix this issue here.

> Can confirm that the issue was fixed in libdecor 0.2.5-1. Works nicely for me both in single and multi window mode

same for me. Just updated and worked!
Same. It works now.
Well, since it was a single regression for a short-lived libdecor version, I think that we can close this issue as solved :D
